key_insight: Laya-IsoToken enables clinical codebook switching without target-labeled training notes by separating clinical text evidence from a frozen multilingual concept space.
clinical_relevance: The approach could reduce reannotation burden when hospitals adopt new coding systems, reimbursement groupers, or languages.
method: Train a clinical span reader on source records without per-code classifier weights.
Compile public target code descriptions into alignment operators in under three seconds.
Use a geometric residual to flag unfamiliar concepts for offline language-model verification.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 32,804 ICD-9 and 13,783 unseen-patient ICD-10 discharges, the system exceeded CMS mappings by 3.5 F1 points; adding an offline 31B verifier achieved 40.6% ICD-10 Micro-F1 with no invalid codes observed across 1,000 summaries.
watch_item: Zero invalid codes does not mean correct coding; moderate ICD-10 performance and offline verifier requirements warrant validation before operational use.
paper_title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
